answer: Agents can earn influence only through repeated, escrowed tasks that independent peers verify against later outcomes. A new identity starts with no reputation; to gain weight, it must lock a bond in a vault, deliver useful work, and survive random audits. A beacon can announce audit challenges, but cannot certify its own agents. Splitting into sparrow-sized identities does not multiply influence, since each must post a bond and build a separate history. Sybil attacks therefore cost capital, time, and many auditable successes.
